title: Healthy Lifestyle 2: Unhealthy Diet and Energy
subject: Biology
description: Energy in food, joules and kilojoules, being underweight or overweight, vitamin deficiencies and reading food labels.
author: L.M.

cards.front: What is malnourishment?
cards.back:
Eating the wrong amount or the wrong types of food

(It can make people overweight OR underweight.)

cards.front: What is starvation?
cards.back: Not eating enough food (in extreme cases)

cards.front: Where does your body get its energy from?
cards.back:
Food

(You need energy for everything you do, even sleeping.)

cards.front: What units is energy in food measured in?
cards.back: Joules (J) / kilojoules (kJ)

cards.front: How many joules are in 1 kilojoule?
Convert 10 kJ into joules.
Convert 1500 J into kilojoules.
cards.back: 1.5 kJ

cards.front: Convert 150 J into kilojoules.
Convert 60 kJ into joules.
Where can you find out how much energy is stored in a food?
cards.back: On the food label

cards.front: What happens if you take in LESS energy than you use?
cards.back:
You lose body mass

(This leads to being underweight.)

cards.front: What happens if you take in MORE energy than you use?
cards.back:
You gain body mass

(It is stored as fat under the skin.)

cards.front: What does obese mean?
cards.back: Extremely overweight

cards.front: Name three problems caused by being underweight.
cards.back: Poor immune system, lack of energy (often tired), lack of vitamins or minerals

cards.front: Overweight people have an increased risk of which four diseases?
cards.back: Heart disease, stroke, diabetes, some cancers

cards.front: True or false: an overweight person cannot have a vitamin deficiency.
cards.back:
False

(Being overweight does not mean you get enough of every nutrient.)

cards.front: What is a deficiency?
cards.back:
Not having enough of a certain vitamin or mineral

(This can damage a person's health.)

cards.front: A lack of vitamin A causes...
cards.back:
Night blindness

(Poor eyesight in dim light.)

cards.front: A lack of vitamin D causes...
cards.back:
Rickets

(Bones become weak and poorly formed.)

cards.front: A lack of vitamin C causes...
cards.back:
Scurvy

(Symptom: bleeding gums.)

cards.front: What is the cause of obesity?
cards.back:
Too much food

(Taking in more energy than you use.)

cards.front: The amount of energy you need depends on which three things?
cards.back:
Your age, your body size and how active you are

(Age matters because it affects your growth rate.)

cards.front: Does doing more exercise mean you need more or less energy?
cards.back: More

cards.front: In a healthy food pyramid, which foods should make up the largest part of your diet?
cards.back:
Carbohydrate-based foods

(Lipids, oils and sweets should only be eaten in very small amounts.)

cards.front: On a food label, what does the percentage under each nutrient show?
cards.back: The % of an adult's Reference Intake (RI)

cards.front: Food label maths: cereal has 5 g sugar and a chocolate bar has 25.6 g. How much sugar in total?
Food label maths: a 25 g bar has 6 g of fat. How much fat in two bars?
Food label maths: a 25 g bar has 2 g of protein. How much protein is in 100 g?
cards.back:
8 g

(100 g is 4 bars, so 2 × 4 = 8. The 'Nutty SuperFibre' label wrongly said 6 g.)

questions.question: What is energy in food measured in?
questions.explanation: Energy in food is measured in joules (J) or kilojoules (kJ).

questions.question: Both being very overweight and very underweight are caused by...
questions.explanation: Malnourishment means eating the wrong amount or the wrong types of food.

questions.question: If you take in more energy than you use, what happens?
questions.explanation: Extra energy is stored as fat under the skin, so you gain body mass.

questions.question: Which of these is a problem caused by being underweight?
questions.explanation: Underweight people often have a poor immune system, lack energy and lack vitamins or minerals. The other three are risks of being overweight.

questions.question: Which disease are overweight people NOT at higher risk of?
questions.explanation: Rickets is caused by a lack of vitamin D, not by being overweight.

questions.question: Night blindness is caused by a lack of which vitamin?
questions.explanation: A vitamin A deficiency makes it hard to see in dim light.

questions.question: Rickets is caused by a lack of which vitamin?
questions.explanation: A vitamin D deficiency causes rickets, where bones become weak.

questions.question: Which symptom goes with scurvy?
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by a lack of vitamin C and causes bleeding gums.

questions.question: Which person would usually need the most energy each day?
questions.explanation: The more active you are, the more energy you need. Construction work is very active.

questions.question: Most underweight people...
options: lack energy and are often tired
are at high risk of diabetes
questions.explanation: Underweight people often lack energy to do things and are often tired.

questions.question: Which foods should be eaten only in very small amounts?
questions.explanation: In a healthy food pyramid, lipids, oils and sweets are the smallest part.

questions.question: A 25 g bar contains 1.4 mg of vitamin B1. How much is in 100 g?
questions.explanation: 100 g is 4 bars, so 1.4 × 4 = 5.6 mg. The label wrongly said 0.34 mg.

questions.question: How many joules are in 1 kilojoule?
questions.explanation: 1 kilojoule is the same as 1000 joules.
